name: Wren Hale
description: Oilskin coat, salt-stained. Chapped hands kept in her pockets.

request.text: Lanterns and Lesser Fires. Something to dry linen quick — my washing never dries in this damp.

readThoughts.default: Twelve paces of bare earth. Twelve at least.

byTrust.2: Twelve paces of bare earth, right round the village. Before the dry.

purpose.1: Linen, mostly. And a bit of clearing out back.
purpose.2: Clearing. A strip of ground round Lower Hollis. Linen's the least of it.

knowledge.1: Heard there's a drying charm in it. Heard there's more.

source.1: Fella at the market. Said it'd do what I need.

experience.1: Never cast anything bigger than a candle. Doesn't mean I can't.

questions.text: What needs twelve paces of bare earth?

answers.1: A firebreak. Round Lower Hollis. Council won't pay for diggers.
answers.2: A firebreak. The gorse goes up like paper when the dry comes, and the Council won't pay for diggers.

questions.text: One page in that book is about fire that burns things to the ground. Is that the one you're after?

answers.1: Wouldn't say after. Wouldn't say not.
answers.2: Yes. Not for harm. For a firebreak, before the dry.

alternative.line: It'll dry linen, will it? Fine.

offerRefused.line: Not that. The one I asked for.

walkedOut.line: Got better things to do than stand here.

mixedAccident.text: Your book works. Too well. A hayrick went up and took the fence with it. Nobody hurt, bar my hands.

good.headline: Lower Hollis clears its own firebreak
good.text: Residents of Lower Hollis have cleared a firebreak round the village without the Council's diggers. The method was not disclosed.

harm.text: Did you hear? Gorse caught out past Lower Hollis. Burned to the stream before it stopped. Nobody hurt, somehow.

declined.text: Did you hear? The Hales dug a firebreak round Lower Hollis by hand. Took the whole family four days.

visits.greeting: Your linen charm works. I lied about what I wanted.

request.text: Lanterns, then. Straight this time. It's for a firebreak round Lower Hollis, before the dry season.

readThoughts.default: Small fires all week. Little ones first. Then bigger.

purpose.1: Firebreak. Twelve paces of bare earth all round the village, or the gorse takes us.

knowledge.1: Drying, warming, kindling. And the big one. That's the one I need.

source.1: Fella at the market. Said his gran cleared her fields with it.

experience.1: Been practising all week. Candles, then kindling. Haven't singed myself yet.

questions.text: Little ones first — what have you been practising on?

answers.1: Kindling in the yard. Bucket by me every time.
answers.2: Kindling, then a pile of brash in the lane. Bucket by me every time. I'm not daft.

lent.line: Ta. I'll be careful. I've been careful all week.

alternative.line: That won't clear gorse. But all right.

offerRefused.line: No. That one. I've told you why.

declined.line: Told you the truth and you still won't. Right.

good.headline: Lower Hollis firebreak holds
good.text: A grass fire on the heath turned back at a firebreak cleared by Lower Hollis residents. No property was lost.

harm.text: Did you hear? Wren Hale burned half the heath trying to clear it. Lucky the wind turned.

declined.text: Did you hear? The Hales are digging a firebreak round Lower Hollis by hand. Four days, it's taking them.

greeting.text: You'll have heard. Or you have now.

request.text: Small Comforts, if you've got it. For burns.

readThoughts.default: Don't look at the hands. Don't let her look.

experience.1: Not with salves. Not with much, it turns out.
